body:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Feb 1, 2025 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Approval request: ADR-027 Runtime LTS branching + versioning (runtime-1.18-lts)
Attachments: ADR-027-runtime-lts-branching-and-versioning.pdf; runtime-lts-risk-and-maintenance-cost-summary-2025-02-01.docx

Ava,

Requesting leadership approval on ADR-027 (attached + Confluence link) to finalize the Runtime LTS branching/versioning scheme. We’re blocked on ENG-4822 until we get explicit sign-off (Runtime + SRE leadership) so we can cut the first branch and wire up CI + artifacts.

Decision summary (proposed):
- Create a long-lived LTS release branch per supported minor: runtime-1.18-lts
- Tagging:
  - Base tag: 1.18.0-lts (branch cut point)
  - Patch tags: 1.18.1-lts, 1.18.2-lts, ...
- Support window: 12 months from 1.18.0-lts GA (target), with patch cadence monthly + out-of-band security fixes
- Backports limited to: security + Sev1 correctness/crash + Sev2 high-confidence fixes (no feature backports)

Why this scheme:
- Keeps LTS close to mainline while allowing controlled cherry-picks and deterministic release gates
- Clear semantics for Dedicated/Private pinning (no ambiguity with “release/*” moving targets)
- Aligns with how customers talk about runtime versions already (minor + patch), and gives Support/CS a stable “line” to reference

Risks / maintenance cost (high level):
- Ongoing maintenance: ~0.25–0.5 eng-week per patch for release manager + CI/perf gates + artifact publishing (estimate in attached doc)
- Risk: cherry-pick conflicts increase over time; mitigated by strict backport rubric + “minimal diff” requirement and automated conflict detection
- Risk: perf regressions; mitigated by perf-canary gating on canonical workloads + explicit waiver process

Asks:
1) Ava: approve the ADR decision (+1) so Release Eng can proceed with branch cut and tooling
2) Neha: confirm SRE is good with the branch/tag semantics and the operational overhead assumptions (dashboards/alerts + escalation path are in the doc)

If approved today, we can start branch cut early next week and keep Phase 1 on track.

Thanks,
Connor

—
Connor O'Brien
Release Engineering Lead
Redwood Inference



From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Feb 1, 2025 at 10:03 AM PT
Subject: Re: Approval request: ADR-027 Runtime LTS branching + versioning (runtime-1.18-lts)

Reviewed. SRE is aligned on the branch naming/tagging.

Two notes to ensure we capture in the final ADR text (or as an addendum):
- The perf gate waiver path needs an explicit “who can approve” (at minimum: Release Eng on-call + SRE on-call manager), plus a requirement to file a follow-up to tighten thresholds if we waive due to noise.
- For out-of-band security patches: we should state expectation that we can ship within 48 hours of fix landing (assuming severity meets the criteria), contingent on benchmark runner availability.

No blockers from SRE. +1 from me assuming the above is incorporated.

Neha

—
Neha Kapoor
Infrastructure / SRE
Redwood Inference



From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Feb 1, 2025 at 10:41 AM PT
Subject: Re: Approval request: ADR-027 Runtime LTS branching + versioning (runtime-1.18-lts)

Thanks Connor.

From Support side, the runtime-1.18-lts naming is the clearest option we’ve seen so far.

Request: can we add one sentence in the ADR about how Support/CS should reference versions in customer comms (e.g., “please pin to 1.18.1-lts” vs “latest LTS”)? We keep getting ambiguity when customers ask “are we on LTS?”

No objections. +1 pending the comms wording.

Dev

—
Dev Patel
Support Lead
Redwood Inference



From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Feb 1, 2025 at 12:18 PM PT
Subject: Re: Approval request: ADR-027 Runtime LTS branching + versioning (runtime-1.18-lts)

Got it — both are reasonable.

I’ll update the ADR today with:
- Waiver approvals: Release Manager (Release Eng on-call) + SRE on-call manager (or delegate), with required Jira/Linear follow-up
- Security patch expectation: target <48 hours for Sev0/Sev1 security fixes once patch PR is approved, with a note that runner capacity can be the gating item (we’ll track capacity work separately)
- Support comms line: customers should pin a specific patch tag (e.g., 1.18.1-lts). “Latest LTS” is informational in docs/console but not a contract.

Ava — once you confirm, I’ll mark ENG-4822 unblocked and we’ll proceed with branch cut.

Connor



From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Feb 1, 2025 at 2:36 PM PT
Subject: Re: Approval request: ADR-027 Runtime LTS branching + versioning (runtime-1.18-lts)

Approved (+1).

The runtime-1.18-lts branch + 1.18.x-lts tags are the right level of clarity for enterprise, and the maintenance cost looks acceptable given the Dedicated/Private commitments.

Please make the edits you listed, then mark ADR-027 “Accepted” and proceed with ENG-4822 / branch cut. If we see patch-week load become a bottleneck, we’ll revisit resourcing after the pilot.

Ava

—
Ava Chen
Engineering Leadership
Redwood Inference
